## Multiple Choice Questions

**1.** Before testing Charles River's journal entries, an auditor compares the total of the JournalEntry table with the journal entry debits in the ledger. Why?

A.  To confirm the tested population is complete before relying on the results
B.  To find the journal entries approved by the same employees who created them
C.  Because a query cannot read the JournalEntry table without first reading GLEntry
D.  To calculate the risk score that Chapter 8 assigned to each journal entry

**2.** An anti-join from the PayrollPayment postings in GLEntry to the PayrollPayment table, on SourceDocumentID, returns six rows. What do they show?

A.  Six payroll payments that were made but never posted to the general ledger
B.  Six employees who were each paid twice for the same pay period
C.  Six payments that were dated before their payroll registers were approved
D.  Six ledger postings that point to a payroll payment that does not exist

**3.** Which test addresses the completeness of the ledger?

A.  An anti-join from GLEntry to a document table, finding postings with no document
B.  A comparison of each supplier invoice's price with the price on its purchase order
C.  An anti-join from a document table to GLEntry, finding documents never posted
D.  A count of the journal entries that were created on a Saturday or a Sunday

**4.** Two queries are combined with UNION ALL, and the second lists its columns in a different order from the first. What happens?

A.  SQLite sorts the columns of both queries by name before it stacks the rows
B.  SQLite stops with an error, because the column names of the queries differ
C.  The values are stacked by position, under the column names of the first query
D.  The rows of the second query are left out, because their columns do not match

**5.** Goods were shipped and delivered on December 6, 2025, and their invoice was posted to the ledger on January 1, 2026. What does this indicate?

A.  The invoice was posted twice, once in each of the two fiscal years
B.  Its revenue was recorded in the wrong fiscal year, a cutoff error
C.  The invoice has no ledger posting and must be traced to its order
D.  The customer paid the invoice before the goods were delivered

**6.** A three-way match compares each goods receipt line with each invoice line, row by row, and reports thousands of mismatches. What is the most likely problem?

A.  Quantities were not summed to the purchase order line before comparing
B.  The invoices were matched to the receipts of a different fiscal year
C.  The receipts were valued at standard cost instead of the order price
D.  The comparison needed a price tolerance instead of a quantity tolerance

**7.** At a price tolerance of 3 percent, no invoice line is an exception; at 2 percent, several thousand are. What should the auditor conclude?

A.  The 2 percent tolerance is correct, because a stricter test finds more exceptions
B.  The 3 percent tolerance is correct, because a test with no exceptions is cleaner
C.  Invoice prices cannot be tested against order prices, because prices change
D.  The tolerance should come from the purchasing policy, set before the test is run

**8.** Receipts not yet invoiced at year-end are valued within a dollar of the balance of account 2020. What does the agreement show?

A.  Every liability to suppliers at the year-end has been recorded in the ledger
B.  The suppliers have billed Charles River for every receipt of the year
C.  The ledger's balance is supported by the detail of the open receipts
D.  The purchase orders behind the receipts were approved within their limits

**9.** On 49 days of fiscal 2026, every manufacturing employee clocked the same hours at the same minutes, and one manager approved all of the overtime. What should the auditor conclude?

A.  The time may have been entered in bulk, so the hours need corroboration
B.  The overtime is proven false and should be removed from the payroll cost
C.  The pattern is a normal shift schedule and needs no further work
D.  The approvals make the hours reliable, because each day was authorized

**10.** One executive approved nearly all of Charles River's purchase orders over three years. What does this indicate?

A.  The purchase orders were all approved above the executive's approval limit
B.  The approvals were made after the executive's employment had ended
C.  Nothing, because an approval by a senior executive is always sufficient
D.  A concentration that can indicate a weakness in the design of the control

**11.** No time clock entry with half an hour of overtime or less has an approval, while nearly every longer one does. What should the auditor do?

A.  Report every short overtime entry as an exception in the audit report
B.  Treat the pattern as an error in the data and leave the entries out of the test
C.  Confirm the policy threshold with payroll, then test the longer entries
D.  Ask the payroll department to remove the short entries from the payroll

**12.** The share of direct labor recorded after its work order operation had ended rose to about two-thirds in fiscal 2026. What does this mean for the controller's analysis?

A.  The manufacturing variance is overstated by about two-thirds of its amount
B.  The operation records cannot show which operations the direct time belongs to
C.  The employees were paid for about two-thirds more time than they worked
D.  The standard costs were set too high and should be reduced for fiscal 2027

**13.** A self-join finds pairs of payments to the same supplier for the same amount. Why does it include the condition `b.DisbursementID > a.DisbursementID`?

A.  It keeps only the payments that were made after the supplier's first invoice
B.  It lists each pair once and never pairs a payment with itself
C.  It makes the query faster by reading the payments in order of their IDs
D.  It removes the payments whose amounts were entered more than once

**14.** Why does the first-digit test use `printf('%e', Amount)` rather than the first character of the amount?

A.  Scientific notation starts with the first significant digit, even below $1
B.  `printf` rounds each amount to the nearest dollar before its first digit is read
C.  The first character of an amount below $1 is its decimal point, not a digit
D.  SQLite cannot read the first character of a number that is stored as REAL

**15.** Why should an audit query library record every change to its tests and keep each run's results?

A.  Because SQLite deletes any query that is not saved as a view before closing
B.  Because an uncontrolled library would undermine the evidence it produces
C.  Because each test must be rewritten from the beginning in every period
D.  Because a query returns different results each time it runs on the same data
